title: Symmetry and Matching
intro: Layout techniques that make matched devices see the same process, the same gradients and the same surroundings (Razavi, Sections 19.2.2 to 19.2.5).

blocks.text: Many lithography and processing steps behave differently along different axes, so matched transistors must point the same way. Two parallel arrangements remain: gates in line, or gates side by side. Implants are tilted about 7° (to avoid channeling), so the gate casts an implant shadow on one side, making source and drain slightly asymmetric. With gates in line, both devices are shadowed identically. With gates side by side, each device has different neighbours on its two sides (one sees the other device, the other sees field oxide), so they are not identical; dummy transistors on the outside restore the symmetry.

Symmetry includes the environment: an unrelated wire crossing over only one device of a pair adds mismatch. Copy it over the other device (even as a grounded dummy line) or, better, route it elsewhere. Symmetry also suppresses common-mode noise and even-order distortion.

Large devices (used for low offset) are long enough for process gradients to matter. Splitting each into halves placed diagonally (a cross-quad) cancels linear gradients in both directions, but its wiring is awkward and can create new asymmetries. Placing four halves in a row also works for gradients along that row:

blocks.alt: Top views: a row of four device halves in the order A, B, B, A with dummies at each end above an arrow showing a gradient; and a two by two grid with A and B on the diagonals.
blocks.caption: One-dimensional cross-coupling (ABBA) and a cross-quad.

blocks.text: If a parameter steps by $\Delta$ from one unit to the next, ABBA gives A $= 2C + 3\Delta$ and B $= 2C + 3\Delta$: cancelled. ABAB gives A $= 2C + 2\Delta$ and B $= 2C + 4\Delta$: an error remains. ABBA leaves the inner B units with different neighbours from the outer A units, so dummies go at both ends.

Shallow trench isolation is filled with oxide, which expands differently from silicon, so it stresses the active area and changes the transistor's I/V characteristic. Grounded dummy fingers at each end of a device (or of a finger array) keep the stress away from the active gates, at the cost of extra drain/source capacitance to ground.

The n-well implant scatters off the thick resist and oxide at the well edge, so PMOS devices near the edge see different doping than those in the middle (the well proximity effect). Matched PMOS devices should sit several microns inside the well, all at similar distances from its edges.

Bias currents across a large chip usually come from one bandgap through mirrors. Distributing a gate voltage over a long ground line adds the ground drops directly to $V_{GS}$, giving systematic errors. Distributing currents instead, and mirroring them locally (with bypass capacitors at the destination), puts the wire resistance in series with a current source where it does no harm, at the price of mismatch between the local mirrors. Large systems may use several local references. Orientation must match across separately drawn blocks.

Ratios: because the effective length differs from the drawn one by a poorly controlled amount, ratioed mirrors use equal lengths and integer numbers of identical unit widths. A half-size device can be a full unit with half its source left floating, so its surroundings stay identical.

blocks.title: Common-centroid
blocks.text: A linear gradient raises $V_{TH}$ by 1 mV per µm across a row. Device A occupies positions 0 and 3 µm, B positions 1 and 2 µm (ABBA). Compare the average $V_{TH}$ shift of A and B with an AABB layout.
solution: ABBA: A averages $(0 + 3)/2 = 1.5$ µm, B averages $(1 + 2)/2 = 1.5$ µm: identical, so mismatch is zero.
AABB: A at $(0 + 1)/2 = 0.5$, B at $(2 + 3)/2 = 2.5$: a 2 mV difference.
blocks.answer: ABBA cancels the gradient; AABB leaves 2 mV.

blocks.title: ABAB with an oxide gradient
blocks.text: Four unit halves in a row have $C_{ox}$ rising 0.1% per unit. Find the relative mismatch between the two devices for ABBA and ABAB connections.

blocks.title: Scaling mirror outputs
blocks.text: A reference transistor carries $I_{REF}$. Outputs of $0.5I_{REF}$ and $3I_{REF}$ are needed. How should they be drawn?
solution: Same $L$ for all. Choose a unit width $W_u$: reference 2 units, $0.5I_{REF}$ output 1 unit, $3I_{REF}$ output 6 units, all identical fingers, same orientation, with dummies around the array. (Or reference 1 unit and the half-size output as one unit with half its source floating.)
blocks.answer: Equal L; integer multiples of a unit width.
